title: On‑Prem Cluster Evacuation & Failover — Quick Reference (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, operations‑facing cheat sheet for evacuating nodes, failing over workloads, and executing quick rollback steps during on‑prem Kubernetes maintenance (bare metal & vSphere). It captures common gotchas for Plymouth/Proxy DNS, BMC access, CSI volume handling, and Terraform module toggles used in our on‑prem packaging.

Scope / audience:
- SREs and field engineers executing upgrades or capacity moves for Private deployments.
- Applies to clusters provisioned with the onprem Terraform modules in our repo (metal/vsphere flavors).
- Not a complete runbook — meant to be used alongside the full cluster bootstrap and upgrade playbooks.

High‑level strategy (evacuation + failover):
1) Preflight: confirm control plane availability, etcd quorum, storage snapshots, and reachability to BMC/IPMI.
2) Cordon & drain, with PVC snapshot/sync for stateful workloads.
3) Move load (LB / DNS), switch region/edge routing if supported, or route traffic to dedicated fallback cluster.
4) Validate, then destroy/recreate nodes (or revert Terraform), rejoin to cluster.
5) Post‑upgrade validation and rollback if necessary.

Prerequisites / quick checks (run before touching nodes):
- kubectl config should point to the cluster control plane with cluster-admin role.
- SSH and BMC access to each node (IPMI/BMC credentials in vault).
- Terraform workspace matches the target environment (terraform workspace show).
- Verify etcd healthy: kubectl get --raw /healthz/etcd or ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=... endpoint health.
- Check control plane pod restarts: kubectl -n kube-system get pods -o wide | grep kube-apiserver
- Snapshot PVCs for stateful components: use CSI snapshot class configured for onprem (snapshot-controller + Velero optional).

Minimal preflight command list:
- kubectl get nodes -o wide
- kubectl get pods -A --field-selector=status.phase!=Running
- kubectl get cs
- etcdctl --endpoints=$ETCD_ENDPOINTS endpoint health
- terraform plan -var-file=env.tfvars

Evacuation sequence (node by node):
1) Cordon the node (prevent new pods):
   kubectl cordon NODE_NAME

2) Drain with eviction timeout and local‑ephemeral handling:
   kubectl drain NODE_NAME --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=120 --timeout=15m
   Notes: use --force only when PodDisruptionBudget (PDB) measurement indicates acceptable risk. Increase grace period for heavy stateful pods.

3) For statefulsets using CSI volumes: 
   - Create a VolumeSnapshot: kubectl create -f snapshot-sample.yaml 
   - Wait for snapshot ready: kubectl get volumesnapshot -n NAMESPACE
   - If PV needs to be detached manually on vSphere, run the Unmount/Detach flow (vCenter) — see vSphere detach checklist below.

4) After drain completes, verify no user workloads left: kubectl get pods -o wide --all-namespaces | grep NODE_NAME

vSphere specific notes (detach & failover):
- If volume stuck in Attached state after K8s detach, use vCenter to force detach. Record the disk UUID and node.
- When cold‑migrating VMs, ensure consistent VM tools quiesce and snapshots are not left behind.
- For thick provisioned storage, watch datastore capacity; failover may increase IOPS on remaining hosts.

Bare‑metal specific notes (PXE/IPXE / iPXE):
- If node fails to rebootstrap, check DHCP+TFTP logs on the provisioning gateway.
- Ensure BMC firmware supports remote media for rescue images (we prefer using Ignition + IPXE chain loading).
- For ipxe-boot chains check: iPXE logs, TFTP server uptime, and HTTP 200 for ignition config.

Terraform module toggles & practical snippets (notes for engineers editing modules):
- module.onprem_cluster.enable_bmc = true|false  # set false for airgapped dry runs
- module.node_pool.count = 3
- module.node_pool.maintenance_taints = ["maintenance=true:NoSchedule"]
- variable "boot_mode" { default = "ipxe" } / alternatives: ignition, cloudinit
- vsphere: resource_pool, datastore and allow_unverified_ssl boolean flags are common causes of plan drift in enterprise vCenter installs

Example snippet (as a string in env.tfvars):
- boot_mode = "ipxe"
- node_count = 5
- control_plane_count = 3
- enable_node_pools = true

Upgrade plan (safe path — rolling with canary):
- Phase 0 (planning): choose a maintenance window, notify CS/PGs, capture traffic baselines, create rollback playbook.
- Phase 1 (canary control plane): upgrade one control plane pod/VM (if using external etcd, start with control plane replicas), verify etcd snapshot and quorum.
- Phase 2 (canary worker nodes): cordon/drain a single worker, reprovision, run smoke tests (ingress, key services).
- Phase 3 (batch workers): upgrade in batches (N=2 or ~10% of pool, whichever is smaller). Monitor PDBs and queue length.
- Phase 4 (validation): run load tests that mimic production latency sensitive flows.
- Phase 5: mark as complete and uncordon.

Rollback triggers and quick rollback actions:
- Triggers: etcd leader flapping, >10% pods failing to start on reprovisioned nodes, application 5xx spike sustained > 5m, DNS propagation failure to backup loadbalancers.
- Quick rollback: revert Terraform to previous workspace snapshot (git tag/terraform state backup), or re‑attach old machines using BMC PXE boot to previous image, restore etcd from snapshot if control plane compromised.
- Commands: terraform apply -var-file=prev_known_good.tfvars, or terraform state mv/replace to reintroduce old instances if needed.

PVC / storage considerations (common pitfalls):
- Always snapshot PVs before drain if volume is critical. CSI snapshots are our safety net.
- Some in‑tree volume plugins on old k8s versions do not support detaching cleanly — verify driver version.
- For Postgres/Mongo: ensure follower is promoted and WAL shipping paused before detaching primary disk.

Quick reference command block (copyable):
- Check cluster health: kubectl get componentstatuses || kubectl get cs
- Cordon: kubectl cordon %NODE%
- Drain: kubectl drain %NODE% --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=120 --timeout=15m
- Reboot node via BMC: ipmitool -I lanplus -H %BMC_HOST% -U %USER% -P %PASS% chassis power cycle
- Terraform plan: terraform plan -var-file=%ENV%.tfvars
- Rollback apply: terraform apply -var-file=prev_good.tfvars

Post‑work validation checklist:
- Pods in default/system namespaces are healthy: kubectl get pods -A | egrep -v "Running|Completed"
- Control plane stable: check kube-apiserver metrics and etcd health
- Node labels and taints consistent: kubectl get nodes --show-labels
- Storage: PVs are Bound and no Pending volumes: kubectl get pv,pvc -A
- Ingress/Loadbalancer: confirm external IPs and DNS entries resolved to active nodes/LB

Handover notes for field ops:
- Always attach Slack incident thread and JIRA ticket to changes.
- Keep a persistent terminal (tmux/screen) during upgrades and document each step in the ticket.
- If performing emergency rollback, take a full terraform state backup and etcd snapshot before any destructive action.

Appendix — common failure scenarios and fixes (short):
- Node stuck in Terminating: kubectl patch node <node> -p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":null}}' (use with caution).
- Pod stuck with ImagePullBackOff: check node DNS and registry reachability; if private registries, verify credentials in secret.
- PVC stuck Pending after reattach: inspect storageclass reclaim policy and CSI controller logs.

Known open items (to be expanded in the full playbook):
- Standardize Terraform module outputs for BMC device mapping.
- Add automated preflight script that validates DNS, DHCP, BMC, dataplane latency, and snapshot status in one run.
- Improve documentation for vSphere VM snapshot quiesce best practices.

End of cheat sheet.

Note: This document is a working draft — add concrete ticket links and environment variables before running in production.
